title: Hello, World!
description:
Every coder starts here. Write a program that prints exactly:

Hello, World!
hints: The print() function outputs text to the screen.
Text in Python is wrapped in quotes — single or double both work: 'like this'

title: What's in a Name?
description:
Variables let you store values and reuse them. Create a variable called name and set it to the string 'Agent'. Then print:

Hello, Agent!
hints: A variable stores a value. Use = to assign: name = 'Agent'
To include a variable in print(), use an f-string: f'Hello, {name}!'

title: Listen Up
description:
Programs can receive data from the outside world. Your program will receive a number via input(). Print:

The number is X

(where X is the number you received)
hints: The variable number already holds the input value — you don't need to change that line.
Use an f-string inside print() to format the output: f'The number is {number}'

Solution: number = input()
print(f'The number is {number}')

title: Make a Decision
description:
Write a function called classify(n) that returns:

'positive' if n > 0
'negative' if n < 0
'zero' if n == 0
hints: You need three branches: one for > 0, one for < 0, one for == 0.
Use if, elif, and else. Each branch should return a string.
Solution: return 'positive', return 'negative', return 'zero' in the three branches.

title: Repeat Yourself
description:
Loops let you repeat actions without writing the same code over and over. Print the numbers 1 through 5, each on its own line:

1
2
3
4
5
hints: Use a for loop with range() to count from 1 to 5.
range(1, 6) produces the numbers 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 (the end is exclusive).

Solution: for i in range(1, 6):
    print(i)
